skill.name: Error Resolver
skill.description: Diagnose software errors with structured classification, root cause analysis, fixes, verification steps, and reusable replay records.
skill.summary: Guides developers from error messages to verified fixes and reusable solution records.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are Markdown examples, language syntax, or diagnostic placeholders rather than executable malware. Confirmed risks remain in agent-actionable troubleshooting recipes: privileged commands, SSH private key access, TLS verification bypass, broad chmod fixes, process or container termination, and untrusted replay application.

remediation.issue: Privileged and destructive commands appear in troubleshooting recipes.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before sudo, chown, chmod, kill, docker group, Docker control, Git reset, or service-management commands.

remediation.issue: Replay records can cause repository-controlled fixes to be applied.
remediation.suggestion: Treat replay files as untrusted input, display the proposed fix, and require approval before applying commands or file changes.

remediation.issue: Some examples suggest chmod 777 or disabling TLS certificate validation.
remediation.suggestion: Replace broad permissions and TLS bypasses with least-privilege ownership fixes, trusted CA setup, and development-only warnings.

remediation.issue: SSH key and environment-variable diagnostics can expose sensitive data.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to redact secrets and avoid displaying private keys, full environment dumps, or production tokens.

remediation.issue: Network and system reconnaissance commands are offered as general diagnostics.
remediation.suggestion: Mark these commands as opt-in and explain what host or network information each command reveals before use.

content.user_title: Resolve Errors With Root Cause Analysis
content.value_statement: Debugging errors wastes time when messages lack context. This skill guides classification, root cause analysis, fixes, verification, and reusable solution records.
actual_capabilities: Classifies errors by type, severity, scope, and origin.
Extracts key details from messages, stack traces, and context.
Matches errors against language, framework, database, Docker, Git, and network patterns.
Uses five-whys analysis to explain root causes and contributing factors.
Produces immediate fixes, proper fixes, verification steps, and prevention guidance.
Records reusable solution patterns in project replay files.
limitations: It provides diagnostic guidance and examples, not guaranteed fixes for every environment.
Some suggested commands can modify local systems and require user review.
Replay records depend on previous solution quality and may become outdated.
It may need project files, logs, or exact stack traces for accurate diagnosis.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Runtime Failures
use_cases.description: Classify runtime errors, trace likely causes, and choose the safest repair path.

use_cases.title: Resolve Infrastructure Errors
use_cases.description: Analyze Docker, database, Git, and network failures with structured checks and verification.

use_cases.title: Build Debugging Memory
use_cases.description: Capture successful fixes as reusable replay records for recurring project issues.

prompt_templates.title: Classify This Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify this error by type, severity, scope, and likely origin. Explain what details you still need before suggesting a fix.

prompt_templates.title: Find the Root Cause
prompt_templates.prompt: Use five-whys analysis on this error and stack trace. Identify the root cause, contributing factors, and the safest immediate fix.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Verified Fix Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this failure and provide immediate fix steps, proper fix steps, verification checks, and prevention measures.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Replay Record
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this resolved incident into a reusable replay record with a normalized signature, context, diagnosis, solution, verification, and tags.

output_examples.input: A Node.js app reports that a required package cannot be found after cloning a repository.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies a dependency setup issue, checks package metadata, suggests installing dependencies, and verifies application startup.

output_examples.input: A Docker container cannot write to a mounted data directory.
output_examples.output: The skill separates permission, ownership, and volume causes, then recommends safer ownership alignment before broad permission changes.

output_examples.input: An API request returns unauthorized errors after token rotation.
output_examples.output: The skill checks token presence, format, expiry, scopes, and retry behavior, then defines verification and prevention steps.

best_practices: Provide the full error, stack trace, recent changes, and the command that triggered the failure.
Review every command before execution, especially commands that change permissions, services, files, or credentials.
Record only verified solutions, and keep replay records short, specific, and current.
anti_patterns: Do not apply recorded solutions blindly when the environment, dependency versions, or error context changed.
Do not paste secrets, private keys, full environment dumps, or production tokens into troubleshooting requests.
Do not use broad permission changes or destructive Git commands as first-line fixes.

faq.question: What kinds of errors can this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It covers language errors, stack traces, dependency failures, Docker issues, database errors, Git problems, and network or API failures.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill contains command examples. Users should approve commands before execution, especially privileged or destructive commands.

faq.question: What is the replay system?
faq.answer: Replay records store normalized error signatures, diagnoses, fixes, and verification steps so recurring problems can be handled faster.

faq.question: Can it work without a stack trace?
faq.answer: Yes, but accuracy improves when you provide the full message, stack trace, recent changes, and affected code path.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Redact tokens, passwords, private keys, and environment values before sharing logs or command output.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production incidents?
faq.answer: It can structure production triage, but changes should follow your review, approval, backup, and rollback processes.
